subject: Physics

nodes.text: reflection is when light bounces off a surface instead of passing through it
the normal is an imaginary line drawn perpendicular to the surface at the point where the light hits
the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, both measured from the normal
the incident ray, the reflected ray, and the normal all lie in the same plane
smooth surfaces give clear specular reflection while rough surfaces scatter light in a diffuse reflection
reflection from a smooth mirror is what lets us see an image of ourselves

textbookPhrasings: The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection, and the incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal to the surface all lie in the same plane.
Reflection of light is the phenomenon of bouncing back of light into the same medium after striking a surface.
A ray of light striking a surface is called the incident ray and the ray that bounces back is called the reflected ray.
referenceFacts: Reflection is light bouncing off a surface
The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection
Angles are measured from the normal to the surface
The incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie in the same plane
Rough surfaces produce diffuse reflection by scattering light
A mirror forms an image by reflecting light

whyQuestions.q: Why can you see a clear image in a mirror but not on a painted wall?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: the smooth mirror reflects light in one direction (specular) while the rough wall scatters it (diffuse)

whyQuestions.q: Why do we measure the angles from the normal rather than from the surface itself?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: the normal gives a consistent reference line, and the law of reflection is defined relative to it

whyQuestions.q: Why does a rough surface look bright but form no image?
whyQuestions.expectedIdea: it scatters light in many directions, so light still reaches you but no ordered image is formed

misconceptions: The angle of incidence and reflection are measured from the surface
Rough surfaces do not reflect light at all
Light is absorbed and destroyed when it hits a surface
